result.topic_en: This is a summary page from Novi Commentarii vol. X introducing Euler's 'Elementa calculi variationum' and 'Analytica explicatio methodi maximorum et minimorum'; it recalls the history of the isoperimetric problem and Johann Bernoulli's solution of the brachistochrone.
result.transcription:
go omnibus casibus integratio expedita est censenda; ex quo haec inuestigatio calculo integrali haud leue incrementum attulisse est aestimanda.

II.
Elementa Calculi variationum
et III.
Analytica explicatio methodi Maximorum et Minimorum.
Auctore Leon. Eulero pag. 51. et 94.

Iam ante celeberrimum problema isoperimetricum insignia quaedam specimina huc pertinentia a Geometris sunt edita, cum antiquissimis iam fuerit exploratum, circulum inter omnes alias figuras pari perimetro inclusas maximam aream complecti; quam quidem proprietatem ex circuli natura concluserunt, minime vero ipsam quaestionem directe aggredi sunt ausi, vt inter omnes figuras aequali perimetro terminatas eam inuestigarent, quae maximam aream includeret. Haec scilicet quaestio nimis est ardua, quam vt ante insignem calculi infinitorum promotionem de ea saltem cogitare licuisset. Mox vero primis quasi iactis huius calculi fundamentis ab acutissimo Iohanne Bernoulli quaestio de brachystochronis felicissimo successu est resoluta: quippe qua
Tom. X. Nou. Comm. b inter

items.quote: circulum inter omnes alias figuras pari perimetro inclusas maximam aream complecti
items.english: Among all other figures enclosed by an equal perimeter, the circle encloses the greatest area.

items.quote: vt inter omnes figuras aequali perimetro terminatas eam inuestigarent, quae maximam aream includeret
items.english: To find, among all figures bounded by an equal perimeter, the one that encloses the greatest area.

items.quote: quaestio de brachystochronis felicissimo successu est resoluta
items.english: The question of brachistochrones was resolved with the greatest success, by Johann Bernoulli.
